note: Full run, 58/58 batches, 1,157 tables. confirmed = 2-vote unanimous. Dominant confirmed class = blind paradigm derivation over IRREGULAR/lexicalized verbs (できられる as a potential-of-potential, ある's suppletive negative rendered あらない/あらなかった/あらなくて, 同じな as attributive). Apply needs owner go-ahead; some fixes are slot REMOVALS, not replacements.

findings.issue: The katakana long-vowel mark ー is transliterated as a bare ASCII hyphen, so every romaji row of this item reads 'kopi-...' (kopi-suru, kopi-shimasu, kopi-dekiru, ...). This is not the recorded 'katakana left unromanized' systemic (the katakana IS romanized here) but a chouonpu-as-hyphen artifact; a learner drilling the card sees a punctuation mark where a long vowel belongs. Expected wapuro-consistent 'kopii' (or 'kopī'). Applies to all 19 forms of this item, anchored here on the dictionary form.

findings.suggested: kopiisuru
findings.fix: kopiisuru
notes: Chouonpu U+30FC rendered as ASCII hyphen in all 19 romaji rows; katakana IS romanized here (cf. tesutosuru), so not a recorded systemic. Same bug in 7 other items.

House convention, not an artifact: corpus writes ー as '-' in romaji (226/231 chōonpu vocab rows; vocab:1050590 romaji is 'kopi-'); validate_groundtruth.py norm_ro and render_diff.py explicitly preserve it. 'kopii' would be wapuro for コピイ.

findings.issue: 出来る (できる) is already the potential of する and has no potential of its own. できられる is not a Japanese word — mechanically derived as if 出来る were an ordinary ichidan verb. Drilling it in SRS teaches a non-existent form.

findings.suggested: (remove — できる has no potential form; 出来る itself expresses ability)
findings.fix: (remove — できる has no potential form; 出来る itself expresses ability)
notes: できられる is unattested: できる is already the potential of する, and a lexicalized potential/stative verb blocks further -られる potential.
できる IS する's potential (batch itself lists できる under vocab:1157170 potential); できられる is a potential-of-potential, unattested. Real error.

findings.issue: できる is a stative intransitive verb and takes no passive; できられる is unattested. Note it is byte-identical to the (also invalid) potential entry, confirming blind ichidan derivation.
findings.current: 出来られる / できられる / dekirareru
findings.suggested: (remove — no passive for できる)
findings.fix: (remove — no passive for できる)
notes: Passive is blocked for stative intransitive できる; できられる is unattested (note: ichidan potential=passive homophony is normal, not itself proof of a bug).
Stative intransitive できる has no passive; 出来られる occurs only as criticized honorific られる. Byte-identical to bad potential row = blind ichidan derivation.

findings.issue: できる is non-volitional (expresses ability/coming into being), so the plain imperative できろ is not used in standard Japanese; ability is commanded with 〜できるようにしろ instead.
findings.current: 出来ろ / できろ / dekiro
findings.suggested: (remove — non-volitional verb, no imperative)
findings.fix: (remove — non-volitional verb, no imperative)
notes: できろ is morphologically regular and does occur colloquially as an exhortation (cf. 分かれ！, 早くできろ); pragmatic rarity is not a conjugation error.
できろ is the correct ichidan imperative; non-volitional verbs do take wishful imperatives (晴れろ, 治れ, 早く出来ろ). Pragmatics quibble, not a form/romaji error.

findings.issue: 同じ is morphologically irregular: unlike a true na-adjective it takes NO な before a noun (同じ人, 同じ日, 同じ本). 同じな only appears before のに/ので/んだ (同じなのに). Drilling 同じな as the attributive teaches the single most common learner error with this word.

findings.suggested: 同じ / おなじ / onaji
findings.fix: 同じ / おなじ / onaji
notes: Confirmed at line 348-353: 同じな is the classic learner error. Attributive is bare 同じ (同じ人/同じ日); な only before のに/ので/んだ. Fix as suggested.
Layer A backs it: JMdict 1451750 lists adj-f (prenominal) BEFORE adj-na. 同じ attaches directly (同じ人/同じ日); な only before のに/ので/んだ. Fix as suggested.

findings.issue: 大人 (おとな) is a noun (JMdict: n, adj-no), not a na-adjective. It attaches の attributively (大人の人, 大人の女性), never な in standard usage, so the whole table is generated from the wrong class. Contrast the neighbouring genuine na-adjectives 大丈夫/大切/大好き/好き/嫌, which are correct.

Premise wrong: JMdict 3.6.2 id 1414170 partOfSpeech = [n, adj-no, adj-na]. na_adj is faithfully sourced, same policy as 元気/上手/本当 (all n+adj-na).

findings.issue: Consequence of the wrong class: the attributive of 大人 is 大人の, not 大人な. 大人な X is colloquial/nonstandard (大人な対応) and wrong to drill as the attributive of a noun in an N5 SRS deck.

大人な is dictionary-sanctioned (JMdict adj-na) and widely attested (大人な対応/大人な人). 大人の is an additional adj-no variant, not a correction of the na-attributive.

Layer A tags it v5r-i (irregular godan); negative is suppletive ない. あらない is unattested in modern standard Japanese.

findings.issue: 罰する is a vs-s (single-kanji + する) verb, not a noun+する compound, so the noun+できる rule does not apply. 罰できる / ばっできる is not a word (the reading ばっできる is impossible). The potential is 罰せる (ばっせる); the periphrastic 罰することができる is the safe alternative. Romaji 'baddekiru' merely mirrors the bad kana.

The potential of 達する is 達せる (たっせる) (or the periphrastic 達することができる). Surface, kana and romaji are all wrong.

findings.issue: 関する is a vs-s verb with a bound stem (関 is not a standalone noun), so the noun+できる potential substitution used for regular サ変 compounds does not apply. 関できる / かんできる is not a Japanese word and would drill an error. The vs-s potential follows the 愛する→愛せる / 察する→察せる pattern (the せ- stem is attested in 我関せず), or is expressed periphrastically as 関することができる.

findings.issue: 高速 is lexically a noun (adj-no in JMdict): the natural attributive is 高速の and the copular/な paradigm (高速だ, 高速な, 高速じゃない) is only marginally attested in technical register. Drilling a full na-adjective table here may teach an unnatural pattern. Low confidence — flagged for human lexical triage; no form in the table is morphologically malformed.
